comparison.pre_description: Pre-event imagery shows dry, drought-stressed mixed agricultural land with sparse scrub vegetation, open pasture areas, and active crop fields in varying states of cultivation.
comparison.post_description: Post-event imagery shows significantly increased vegetation greenness consistent with post-storm rainfall saturation, with altered field boundaries, possible inundation of low-lying areas, and changes to vegetation cover extent.
comparison.notes: Primary observable differences include dramatic increase in green vegetation cover post-hurricane suggesting rainfall-driven regrowth or waterlogging, altered appearance of the central open pasture area, changes to the darker scrub/woodland patches in the northeast quadrant, and lower fields showing signs of moisture saturation or shallow flooding; no major structural losses visible as area appears predominantly agricultural/natural land use rather than built environment.

comparison.pre_description: Dense residential neighborhood with intact red/orange rooftops, green vegetation corridors, sports fields, and well-defined street grid across hillside terrain near the Pacific Palisades coastline.
comparison.post_description: Massive destruction visible across the majority of the residential grid, with building footprints reduced to gray ash pads, complete vegetation loss along corridors, and widespread burn scarring replacing formerly intact structures.
comparison.notes: The post-event image shows near-total destruction of residential structures across the central and lower portions of the frame — rooftops are replaced by uniform gray ash/concrete slabs consistent with complete combustion. Vegetation along the canyon/creek corridors is entirely eliminated. The sports fields (football/soccer) remain identifiable but surrounding structures are gone. The upper-right quadrant retains partial structure survival. Burn scar patterns follow topographic wind corridors. Estimated 70%+ of visible residential parcels show complete structural loss.

comparison.pre_description: Pre-event imagery shows a dense residential neighborhood along PCH at Malibu Colony with intact structures, green vegetation including a golf course, and a healthy lagoon ecosystem with clear coastal features.
comparison.post_description: Post-event imagery shows significant loss of building footprints along the beachfront residential strip, widespread vegetation loss, darkened burn scar areas replacing previously green zones, and altered lagoon appearance consistent with fire damage.
comparison.notes: Primary observable differences include: (1) substantial reduction in visible rooftop density along the beachfront residential corridor suggesting structure destruction, (2) green golf course and hillside vegetation significantly reduced and darkened indicating burn scarring, (3) lagoon area shows altered coloration and reduced vegetative buffer, (4) hillside areas northeast of PCH show extensive vegetation removal consistent with wildfire burn patterns, (5) overall scene brightness and color signature shift indicates widespread combustion across the study area

comparison.pre_description: A dense coastal residential neighborhood with multi-story homes, mature vegetation, green landscaping, and tree canopy covering hillsides above Pacific Coast Highway near Las Tunas Beach.
comparison.post_description: Widespread burn scarring has consumed nearly all hillside vegetation, numerous building footprints show loss or severe damage, and the landscape is reduced to bare brown earth with only a cluster of structures remaining in the western portion of the neighborhood.
comparison.notes: Hillside vegetation has been almost entirely eliminated, transitioning from dense green chaparral to bare burned terrain. Significant reduction in visible building rooftops in the eastern and upper portions of the neighborhood; remaining structures in the western cluster appear partially intact. The coastal road corridor (PCH) remains visible but surrounding areas show extensive fire damage consistent with the Palisades Fire burn pattern. Large areas east of the residential cluster show complete vegetation loss and potential soil exposure indicating high-intensity fire passage.

comparison.pre_description: Dense residential neighborhood in Pacific Palisades with intact red-roofed homes, green vegetation, a blue athletic track, and a well-defined coastal community along the beach.
comparison.post_description: Widespread destruction across the neighborhood with massive building footprint loss, extensive burn scars replacing vegetation, collapsed structures reduced to ash/debris fields, and near-total destruction of the coastal mobile home and residential areas.
comparison.notes: The lower coastal residential zone (mobile homes/beach community) shows near-complete destruction with only structural foundations/debris remaining; the hillside residential areas in the northwest quadrant show heavy burn scarring and vegetation loss replacing formerly green tree canopy; the mid-section residential blocks show significant structure loss with gray ash-colored footprints replacing intact homes; the athletic track and upper commercial areas appear comparatively less damaged; burn scar boundary is clearly visible contrasting intact eastern neighborhoods; estimated 60-70% of structures in frame are destroyed or severely damaged.
